stories.title: Pompeii, buried by Vesuvius in AD 79
stories.summary: UNESCO says the eruption of Vesuvius in AD 79 buried Pompeii, mostly under ash and lapilli; it has been excavated since the mid-18th century and was inscribed in 1997.

location.name: Pompeii (approximate site centre)
location.note: Pleiades place 433032 representative point (CC BY 3.0); Wikidata Q43332 agrees within 0.38 km. A site centre, not a boundary.

stories.script: UNESCO says Mount Vesuvius erupted in AD 79 and buried the Roman town of Pompeii, mostly under volcanic ash and lapilli. The town has been excavated bit by bit since the mid-18th century, and it was inscribed on the World Heritage List in 1997, together with Herculaneum and Torre Annunziata. The pin is an approximate site centre.

captions.text: Buried by Vesuvius under ash and lapilli.
Excavated since the mid-1700s. Listed in 1997.

cards.title: Pompeii
cards.body: UNESCO's World Heritage page (list 829) says that when Vesuvius erupted in AD 79 it engulfed the Roman towns of Pompeii and Herculaneum; Pompeii was buried largely by volcanic ash and lapilli. Both have been progressively excavated and opened to the public since the mid-18th century. Pleiades records Pompeii as destroyed by the eruption of AD 79.
